classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the average loss based on original value from successive daily multipliers, then recover the fourth-day loss using its different base.

content.prompt: Particular shares were released in the stock market and lost, per day, an average of $2.23\%$ of their original value over the first four days. Over the first day, the shares increased in value by $15\%$, and over the second day, a further $10\%$ increase was recorded. However, a $20\%$ decrease in the share value occurred on the third day. What percentage decrease was recorded over the fourth day?

answer.short:
$10\%$ decrease.

The four-day loss is based on the original value; the fourth-day decrease is based on the value after day three.
answer.worked:
Take the original value as $100$ units. The average loss is stated as a percentage of this original value.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total four-day loss}&=4\times2.23\\\text{Total four-day loss}&=8.92\\\text{Value after day four}&=100-8.92\\\text{Value after day four}&=91.08\\\text{Value after day three}&=100\times1.15\times1.10\times0.80\\\text{Value after day three}&=101.2\\\text{Fourth-day percentage decrease}&=\frac{101.2-91.08}{101.2}\times100\%\\\text{Fourth-day percentage decrease}&=10\%\end{align*}$$
